claims.text: Adding 2–5 wt% silicon during synthesis will promote formation of a stable, Si-rich passive surface film.
The proposed Si-rich passive film is likely composed of silica.
Formation of the Si-rich film will significantly reduce molten-aluminum corrosion relative to undoped boride alloys.
Boride alloy components without silicon enrichment are susceptible to direct chemical attack by molten aluminum.
A 2–5 wt% silicon addition can be incorporated into the boride alloy through melt alloying and controlled casting.
Controlled cooling will produce a uniform silicon distribution in the boride alloy.
A continuous Si-enriched film will form in situ during an initial oxidation stage in the operating environment.
Alloyed silicon will oxidize preferentially at the component surface.
Preferential silicon oxidation will form a durable silica layer.
The silica layer will act as a physical and chemical barrier to contact between molten aluminum and the boride matrix.
Blocking contact between molten aluminum and the boride matrix will inhibit the corrosion reaction.
Silicon-doped boride components will have lower weight loss than undoped components after identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Silicon-doped boride components will retain greater surface and microstructural integrity than undoped components.
Undoped boride components typically exhibit higher weight loss and surface degradation after exposure to molten aluminum at 750°C.
The protective film is expected to remain effective around 750°C for exposure durations up to 24 hours.
Nonuniform silicon distribution or phase inhomogeneity may compromise corrosion protection.
